title: Ledgers & posting
examples: Can you show me how to balance an account?
What is the difference between posting and balancing?
If I have a debit balance, does that mean I have money or I owe money?

explain.say: Today we are learning about balancing accounts in the ledger.
First we look at the debit side of an account.
Next we look at the credit side of an account.
To balance, we must make sure the totals match.
If the debit total is higher, that is the balance carried down.
In real life, a bank statement needs balancing too.

faq.q: What does it mean for an account to be 'balanced'?
faq.a: It means the total amount recorded on the debit side equals the total amount on the credit side. You can also ask what it means to make an account balance.
asks: How do I balance the ledger?
What is the goal when balancing an account?

faq.q: If the debit side is bigger, what do I do?
faq.a: If the debit side is bigger, you write the difference as a 'balance carried down' on the credit side. You might also ask what to do if the debit side is larger.
asks: How do I show a debit balance?
What is the balance if debit is higher?

faq.q: Do I always use debit and credit?
faq.a: Yes, in double-entry bookkeeping, every transaction affects at least two accounts, one on the debit and one on the credit. Can I use debit and credit for everything?
asks: Is debit always money coming in?

faq.q: What is the difference between posting and balancing?
faq.a: Posting is recording the transaction into the correct ledger account. Balancing is calculating the final total and the remaining balance of that account. What is the difference between posting and balancing?
asks: When do I balance the ledger?

faq.q: What if I don't know which side is debit or credit?
faq.a: You must remember that assets and expenses usually increase on the debit side. You could ask me what increases on the debit side.
asks: How do I know which side to post to?

facts: Assets and expenses typically increase on the debit side.
Liabilities and capital usually increase on the credit side.
The fundamental rule is that total debits must equal total credits.
Balancing involves calculating the difference between the two sides.

quiz.say: If a business buys equipment using cash, which account increases on the debit side?
quiz.why: Equipment is an asset, and assets increase on the debit side.

wrong.0: Sales revenue is income, and it increases on the credit side.
wrong.2: Cash decreases when you buy something, so it should be on the credit side.
wrong.3: Accounts Payable is a liability, and liabilities increase on the credit side.

quiz.say: A business owes money to its suppliers. This is recorded as an increase in which account?
quiz.why: Accounts Payable is a liability, and liabilities increase on the credit side.

wrong.1: Cash is an asset; an increase would be on the debit side.
wrong.2: Purchases are expenses, which increase on the debit side.
wrong.3: While capital is a liability, the specific account for suppliers is Accounts Payable.
